definitions.explanation: Being alone or going somewhere without companions. Often refers specifically to living or working away from one's family.

examples.japanese: {単身|たんしん}で{海外|かいがい}に{渡|わた}った。
{父|ちち}は{大阪|おおさか}に{単身赴任|たんしんふにん}している。
examples.english: My father is on a solo work transfer in Osaka.

examples.japanese: {単身|たんしん}{世帯|せたい}{向|む}けのマンションが{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Apartments for single-person households are increasing.

notes:
{単身|たんしん} can function as both a noun and an adverb. It is commonly used in compound expressions related to living or working alone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {単身赴任|たんしんふにん} (solo work transfer — living apart from family for work)
- {単身|たんしん}{世帯|せたい} (single-person household)
- {単身|たんしん}{者|しゃ} (a person living alone)
- {単身|たんしん}で{乗|の}り{込|こ}む (to go in alone)

USAGE:
{単身赴任|たんしんふにん} is one of the most frequently used compounds. It refers to the common Japanese practice where a worker is transferred to a distant office and lives alone while the family stays behind, typically so that children can continue at the same school.
